evidence.observation: The plan says "(a) U4–U7 ask nothing of it. The span walk still re-hashes and counts it when it names a document the root declares, and ignores it otherwise." and "U4–U7 ask nothing of an included element." In _unattended.py:285-293, _span_walk adds every visited span to total and adds to rehashed only when _span_issue(...) returns None. A span whose digest names a supplied, declared document but has start >= end is counted and never re-hashed. A non-unattended included file can carry such a span: _unattended.py:324-325 says 'outside the mode, layer one does not check provenance.spans'. Today U7 refuses that root with 'a span needs 0 <= start < end'. Under VG3 U7 is exempt, so the only symptom left is the unattended:spans-unchecked error 'supply every declared document with --document', which is raised under --require-documents even when every document was supplied.

concerns.recommendation: Have D14 say what happens to an included span that names a declared document but whose shape _span_issue refuses: counted with a named diagnostic, or ignored like a span over another document. Add that case to VG3-C5.
concerns.title: D14 counts a malformed included span as unchecked, which gives a misleading --require-documents error once U7 is exempt

evidence.observation: D5 promises "and the `includes[ID]:` prefix on every diagnostic", and VG3-C8 says "This tests the function over a synthetic issue". Under D14 (a), included spans over a root-declared document are re-hashed. Their diagnostics (unattended:excerpt-mismatch, unattended:span-out-of-range) come from commands/checking.py:84-85, which runs over result.model.model_dump(). Only _model_warnings (model/__init__.py:302-305) calls remap_issues, so these issues keep composed addresses: an included top-level constraint shows as $.constraints[k], with k offset by the root's own constraints, and no include prefix. No VG3 criterion covers a span-walk diagnostic on an included element.

concerns.recommendation: Send the span-walk issues of an include root through remap_issues. The origins are already on model._provenance (model/__init__.py:317). Add a criterion: an included span over a root-declared document with a wrong excerpt_sha256 exits 3 under includes[ID]:.
concerns.title: Re-hash diagnostics on included spans bypass remap_issues, so D5's 'every diagnostic' prefix is neither met nor tested

evidence.location: section 5 Compatibility; section 10 open questions; section 4 VG3-C10
evidence.observation: Section 5 says "No schema version changes." The open questions leave "the attribution lines' exact text, in text and in JSON" to the spec, and VG3-C10 says "the attribution lines are the only new output (D14)". The docstring of payloads.py:693-705 build_validate_payload says the payload 'Stays on the frozen variants ... widening `validate` would move a payload nobody asked to move (IF-P3-5)'. The payload holds only issues and warnings, and ValidationIssue severity is error or warning. JSON attribution must therefore either widen a frozen payload or ride as warning entries on every unattended include root. The plan picks neither.

concerns.recommendation: Choose the JSON carrier in the plan: a payload field (and say whether that counts as a schema or variant change), warning entries, or no JSON attribution. Make section 5 and VG3-C10 state the same choice.
concerns.title: JSON attribution conflicts with the frozen validate payload and with 'no schema version changes'

evidence.location: section 10, D4 row; section 6 U1 risk row; section 4 VG4-C3
evidence.observation: D4 proposes "(a) U1 admits no documents while the root declares nothing but its header and its includes (§2)", and section 6 says "U1 stays whenever any section of the root other than its header and `includes` holds an entry". A model with no includes meets that test. An unattended model of any version that holds only version, model_id and source with reviewer none and no documents would now validate; today U1 refuses it with 'must declare at least one source document' (_unattended.py:85-86). D4 asks about #222 case 3, which is an include root, and every VG4-C3 case is a root. Nothing says whether the relaxation requires includes, and no case covers a model without them.

concerns.recommendation: State whether the first-document rule applies only when includes is present. Add a VG4-C3 case for an unattended model with no includes, no documents and no elements, with the outcome chosen.
concerns.title: D4's first-document rule also admits an empty unattended model with no includes, and the plan does not say if that is intended

evidence.observation: The plan says "\"Owns\" is the origin test VG3 uses, written once", while section 2 also says the rule "is written on the file". H16 says "`_rule_unattended` takes the document alone", and that document is the composed one. _includes.py:_merge has already extended object_types, fact_types, constraints and deontic_notes with the included elements (SECTIONS, _includes.py:33,138). Read on that composed document, 'every section other than the header and includes is absent or empty' is false for every #222 case 3 root. The origin test also has no origin entries for rejected_proposals or reference_populations, because _ids (_includes.py:119-127) does not walk them.

concerns.recommendation: Say whether U1 reads the root's own bytes before the merge or applies the origin test to the composed document. If it is the origin test, say that rejected_proposals and reference_populations are root-owned by construction, since R0.5 forbids them in an include.
concerns.title: The first-document rule is 'written on the file', but U1 runs over the merged document

evidence.observation: Section 6 says "A host that can write both the root and an include can carry any claim, `confirmed` and `alethic` ones too `(p1)`" and "Those are counts; they do not list each element or each combination `(s2)`." An include can also carry sample_population rows on its fact types: _merge copies fact_types whole (_includes.py:138). Under VG3 those rows owe nothing to U6, and their sample_spans are ignored when they name a document the root does not declare (D14). Neither D5's counts nor the stated limit mention sample rows, so the attribution line gives a reader no sign that sample data came through the pin.

concerns.recommendation: Name sample rows in the section 6 limit and the 'Unattended source' text. Consider adding a sample-row count to the D5 attribution line.
concerns.title: Sample rows an include carries are left out of both the attribution counts and the stated limit

evidence.observation: Section 8 still says "one round is planned, a second only if the first blocks." The status paragraph says "Both planned rounds are spent (§8).", and the third bullet of section 8 says the budget was two rounds.

concerns.recommendation: Replace the r1 sentence in section 8 with the two-round budget the next bullet states.
concerns.title: Section 8 still states r1's one-round budget

response.summary: Plan r3 has no blocking concern. The cited lines for H13, H27 and H31-H35 match the checkout: _unattended.py:58/193/204-234, _includes.py:162-167/222-241 and project.md:129-131. VG3-C9 can be tested because D-03 on a proposed llm-inferred alethic constraint is only a warning (_validation.py:1440-1450), so such an include is standalone-valid, and a confirmed llm-inferred constraint passes semantic:status-source. The first-document rule names every top-level property of orm-meta.schema.json, which has additionalProperties false, so a root with a claim of its own cannot escape it. VG3-C2 and VG3-C3 together cover U2-U8 on root-owned elements. Every lane file in section 9 exists. The open points are in D14's span walk (malformed included spans, and diagnostics that skip remap_issues), the JSON carrier for D5's attribution against the frozen validate payload, the scope and evaluation point of D4's rule, the content an include carries that attribution leaves out, and one stale sentence in section 8.

evidence.location: Goal and completion predicates, VG3 and VG5
evidence.observation: The plan requires: “A version-5 root with `source.mode: unattended` that includes a reviewed, non-unattended model validates, exit 0” and “One packaged example runs the whole path: a reviewed seed, an unattended root that includes it, two growth rounds”. Together, these predicates require the reviewed seed to remain included.

The plan says: “If D3 is ruled (b), VG3 becomes a documentation phase, VG4 shrinks to D4, and VG5's example uses the imported packaging of H25.” D3 (b) is to “keep today's refusal”, so this fallback cannot satisfy the stated VG3 and VG5 predicates.

concerns.recommendation: If the owner selects D3 (b), require a plan amendment that replaces the VG3 and VG5 completion predicates and their tests before phase execution. Otherwise, remove the fallback as an executable path.
concerns.title: D3 (b) fallback leaves the milestone’s completion predicates unattainable

response.summary: The proposed D3 (a) path is coherent, but the specified D3 (b) fallback cannot meet the plan’s unchanged completion predicates.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
For this plan, a concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented or tested as written, or the milestone would not do what its goal claims.

Their records are .gnd-planning/milestones/reviewed-vocabulary-growth/evidence/plan-review-r1/disposition.md and .gnd-planning/milestones/reviewed-vocabulary-growth/evidence/plan-review-r2/disposition.md and may be read for context. In the plan, (p1) marks a repair from round 1, (s2) a repair from one of the two single reviews of round 2, and (m) a change by the author that no reviewer asked for. Do not restate a concern that r3 repairs. Report an earlier concern again only if its repair is wrong or incomplete, and say which.

Is each (p1) and (s2) repair correct against the repository at this checkout and consistent with the rest of the plan? In particular: obligations H30 to H36 and the corrected H13 and H27 (read the cited lines in src/gnd, tests and .codex/skills/process-phase/references/project.md before reporting a mismatch); criteria VG1-C7, VG1-C8, VG3-C2, VG3-C3, VG3-C5, VG3-C8, VG3-C9, VG3-C10 and VG4-C3; and the D2 (b) readings of VG2 and VG5.

D13 proposes that an included element of an unattended root is exempt from U2 to U7, and from U8 only when its status is confirmed, with the root's pin as the statement of review and the remaining trust named as a limit in section 6. D14 proposes that a span an included element carries is still re-hashed and counted when it names a document the root declares, and ignored otherwise. Are both proposals implementable and testable as written, do they agree with src/gnd/model/_unattended.py, src/gnd/model/_includes.py and src/gnd/commands/checking.py, and do they keep the output of an unattended include root that validates today (H30)? Section 2 now writes the first-document rule of D4 (a) on the file: every section of the root other than version, model_id, source and includes is absent or empty. Does that leave any way for a root with a claim of its own to validate with no source document, and does it refuse anything it should admit? Check it against src/gnd/schema/orm-meta.schema.json and src/gnd/model/_includes.py.
Do sections 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 still agree with each other after the repairs? Name any criterion, decision, home or lane that r2 left stale, contradictory or untestable.
